mission.title: Install and Configure k0s (Zero Friction Kubernetes)
mission.description: k0s is a lightweight, all-inclusive Kubernetes distribution designed for simplicity and ease of use. It is ideal for users looking to quickly bootstrap Kubernetes clusters on any cloud, bare metal, or edge environments. The trade-off is that while it simplifies installation, users may need to manage certain configurations manually.

steps.title: Install the k0s binary
steps.description:
This step installs the k0s binary on your system, which is required to manage your Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

curl -sSL https://github.com/k0sproject/k0s/releases/download/v1.31.0/k0s-v1.31.0-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/k0s

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k0s

```

> Download the k0s binary
> Make the k0s binary executable

steps.title: Initialize the k0s controller
steps.description:
This command initializes the k0s controller, which is the master node of your Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

k0s init --enable-worker

```

> Initialize the cluster and enable worker nodes

steps.title: Start the k0s controller
steps.description:
This command starts the k0s controller, allowing it to manage the Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

k0s start

```

> Start the k0s controller

steps.title: Verify the cluster is running
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure everything is running correctly.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> Verify that the nodes are in a Ready state

uninstall.title: Uninstall k0s
uninstall.description:
This step removes the k0s installation and all associated resources. Be aware that this will delete all Kubernetes resources and data.

```bash

k0s stop

rm -rf /var/lib/k0s

```

> Stop the k0s controller
> Remove all k0s data

upgrade.title: Upgrade k0s
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your cluster configuration. This step upgrades the k0s binary and restarts the controller.

```bash

k0s stop

curl -sSL https://github.com/k0sproject/k0s/releases/download/v1.31.0/k0s-v1.31.0-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/k0s

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k0s

k0s start

kubectl get nodes

```

> Stop the k0s controller before upgrading
> Download the latest k0s binary
> Make the new k0s binary executable
> Restart the k0s controller
> Verify that the nodes are still in a Ready state

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'k0s: command not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The k0s binary is not installed or not in your PATH.

**Fix:**
Ensure that the k0s binary is installed and located in /usr/local/bin or another directory in your PATH.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'k0s controller is not running'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The k0s controller has not been started or has crashed.

**Fix:**
Run 'k0s start' to start the controller and check logs for errors.

troubleshooting.title: kubectl get nodes shows 'NotReady'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The nodes may not have joined the cluster correctly.

**Fix:**
Check the k0s logs for errors and ensure the nodes are properly configured.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubelet not running'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubelet service may not be running on the worker nodes.

**Fix:**
Check the kubelet service status and restart it if necessary.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for multi-architecture images, improved logging capabilities.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated the old configuration format in favor of a new YAML-based format.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from v1.30, convert your configuration to the new YAML format.

resolution.summary: You should see output similar to 'NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION' with nodes listed as 'Ready' when running 'kubectl get nodes'.

prerequisites.description: Ensure you have a Linux environment with the necessary resources.
